reason: The cited evidence directly supports the nanocluster segregation mechanism (E3) and the precipitate-engineering strategy (E4), but the claim that precipitates 'maintain grain boundary integrity and ductility' is slightly overstated relative to the evidence, which shows improved ductility but not full preservation of the baseline properties.
premises: Principal elements (Ni, Cr, Mn) rapidly segregate to grain boundaries as nanoclusters in single-phase HEAs at intermediate temperatures
These nanoclusters reduce grain boundary cohesion and promote intergranular fracture
Pre-existing, embrittling-element–rich precipitates at grain boundaries can absorb segregating elements
Absorption by precipitates prevents harmful segregation and preserves ductility
